hero.title: Transforming Albanian Trade
hero.subtitle: The National Single Window (NSW) — the single electronic entry point for all cross-border trade regulatory requirements in Albania.

whatIsNsw.title: What is the National Single Window?
whatIsNsw.description: The National Single Window (NSW) is an electronic platform that enables traders to submit their data only once through a single entry point. The NSW automatically distributes this data to all relevant regulatory agencies, eliminating multiple submissions and streamlining the cross-border trade process.
whatIsNsw.description2: Supported by the World Bank and operated by NAIS (National Agency for Information Society), the NSW represents a decisive step toward modernizing Albania's trade infrastructure and aligning with European Union standards.
whatIsNsw.feature1Desc: Submit your data just once. The NSW automatically distributes it to the relevant agencies.
whatIsNsw.feature2Desc: Track the status of your application in real-time, at every step of the process.
whatIsNsw.feature3Desc: Parallel processing by regulatory agencies, significantly reducing clearance time.

aboutPage.title: About the National Single Window
aboutPage.subtitle: Modernizing cross-border trade in Albania
aboutPage.whatIsNsw1: The National Single Window (NSW) is an electronic system that enables parties involved in trade and transport to submit standardized information and documents at a single entry point to fulfill all regulatory requirements related to import, export, and transit.
aboutPage.whatIsNsw2: Through the NSW, traders no longer need to physically visit multiple government agencies or submit the same data multiple times. The system collects information once and automatically distributes it to the relevant agencies for processing.
aboutPage.whatIsNsw3: Albania's NSW is operated by NAIS (National Agency for Information Society) under the oversight of the Ministry of Economy and Innovation, with financial support from the World Bank.
aboutPage.whatIsNsw4: The project aims to significantly improve the efficiency of trade procedures, reduce costs for businesses, and support Albania on its path toward European Union membership.
aboutPage.vision: An Albania where cross-border trade is fast, transparent, and fully digital — contributing to economic growth and European integration.
aboutPage.mission: To digitize and simplify the cross-border trade process by providing a single electronic entry point for all regulatory requirements, reducing time, costs, and bureaucratic barriers.
aboutPage.legalBasis: The NSW is based on the following legal and regulatory framework:
aboutPage.legalItem1: Law on the National Single Window of the Republic of Albania
aboutPage.legalItem4: EU Customs acquis — alignment with European standards
aboutPage.governanceSubtitle: The NSW is governed through three institutional layers:
aboutPage.govLayer1Desc: Private sector, regulatory agencies (CBRAs), domain experts — provide advice and feedback
aboutPage.govLayer2Desc: NSW Steering Committee — makes strategic decisions and oversees progress
aboutPage.govLayer3Desc: NSW Operator (NAIS/AKSHI) — implements and maintains the platform
aboutPage.timeline1Event: Signing of the World Bank agreement for NSW financing
aboutPage.timeline2Event: Project implementation start and Steering Committee establishment
aboutPage.timeline3Event: Technical architecture completion and development start
aboutPage.timeline4Event: Pilot phase with initial regulatory agencies
aboutPage.timeline5Event: Full NSW launch with all 8 regulatory agencies
aboutPage.fundingDesc: The NSW project is financed in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, under the Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation Project – Albania. The project is financed through Loan No. IBRD 89330, and the procurement process was based on Request for Proposals (RFP) No. WBTTF-ALB-112CDEF. This financing supports the development of the NSW platform, capacity building, and technical assistance.
aboutPage.euDesc: As an EU candidate country, Albania is actively working to align its regulatory framework with European standards. The NSW is a key component of this effort, ensuring that Albania's cross-border trade procedures are compatible with the EU customs acquis and international best practices.

howItWorksPage.title: How NSW Works
howItWorksPage.subtitle: The step-by-step process of cross-border trade through NSW
howItWorksPage.step1Desc: The trader registers on the NSW platform and creates their account.
howItWorksPage.step2Desc: The trader submits the application (LPCO) only once through the NSW.
howItWorksPage.step3Desc: The NSW automatically distributes the data to the relevant regulatory agencies.
howItWorksPage.step4Desc: Regulatory agencies (CBRAs) process the application simultaneously.
howItWorksPage.step5Desc: If inspection is required, the NSW coordinates the process between agencies.
howItWorksPage.step6Desc: The decision is communicated through the NSW — approval, rejection, or request for additional information.
howItWorksPage.step7Desc: Clearance information is automatically sent to Customs (ASYCUDA).
howItWorksPage.step8Desc: Goods are released for import, export, or transit after all procedures are completed.
howItWorksPage.onceOnlySubtitle: How NSW changes the trade process
beforeItems: Submits the same data multiple times
howItWorksPage.lpcoDesc: LPCO represents four types of regulatory documents required for cross-border trade:
howItWorksPage.lpcoL: License — Permission for specific trade activities
howItWorksPage.lpcoP: Permit — Authorization for importing/exporting certain goods
howItWorksPage.lpcoC: Certificate — Verification of compliance with standards
howItWorksPage.integrationDesc: The NSW integrates with existing government systems, including ASYCUDA World (customs system) and e-Albania, ensuring a seamless flow of information between all parties.
